note: Pins RATIFIED v3. EXPECTED-RED: no engine implements these gates yet -- there is no food-suitability entry point in the published interface, so this slice has no runner until one exists. Belongs to a FOOD-COMPOSITION bundle, NOT pre-workout-macros@v1 (that manifest explicitly excludes this slice). Expected is an engine-agnostic verdict per section 11 ('deliberately not tied to any engine interface'): {verdict, failedGate: H1..H7|null, knownException}. Two extensions, both documented: failedRule='matrix' for a section 3.10 tier-matrix rejection, which is a Layer A membership rule and has no H-number; and {available, rating} for the pure matrix-coverage vectors. A feeding is evaluated on its SUMMED macros, never per item (check 4). Gate evaluation order is an ORACLE CONVENTION -- matrix, H4, H5, H6, H1, H2, H3, H7 -- because the SSOT specifies none; every section 7 example fails at most one gate so the order does not affect them. Macro values for the section 7 feedings are taken verbatim from that table, not re-derived from USDA; food-to-macro lookup is a separate food-database concern. toleranceG applies to gram-vs-ceiling comparisons; '<=' is inclusive.

The doc states this explicitly: at 95 kg H3 rises to 38 g, so the 31.2 g plate that fails at 65 kg passes. Same feeding, different mass, opposite verdict -- the scaling is real, not cosmetic.

The floor's whole purpose: a straight 0.12 g/kg would cap fibre at 6.0 g at 50 kg and reject oatmeal-plus-banana (7.1 g). max(8, per-kg) keeps it at 8.0 and it passes. Regression guard against reintroducing v1's over-restriction.
S1 advisory only: 1200 kcal is far above 4 x 120 min, yet every hard gate passes, so the verdict is PASS. Calorie count is explicitly not a gate and must never become one (check 2).
Same property at the top-off: a large-energy drink inside the 8 % ceiling passes. No gate reads kcal.

The 2 oz chicken variant the doc names as passing (22.4 g protein against 26 g). Carbohydrate is NOT the dominant energy source here; S2 has no floor and must not reject it. This is the exact shape v1 got wrong. Fat/fibre carried from the 3 oz plate as a conservative upper bound.

Two slices of whole-wheat bread: 3.8 g fibre passes H2's 8 g meal ceiling. G8 is LIMITED (not AVOID) at the meal tier, so it is available. S3's refined-over-whole preference is a soft score and must not reject it -- the doc says outright that H2's grams do not separate G1 from G8.
A teaspoon of mustard: 0.2 g fat reads 47 % of energy from fat, but no percentage may be evaluated below 50 kcal (section 4, check 5). Gram gates all pass, so PASS.
Black coffee reads 100 % protein by energy. Under 50 kcal no percentage is evaluated; nothing rejects it at the meal tier (H5 is top-off-only).

9 % sustained with no chase water and no bolus claim -- FAIL H6 against the 8 % ceiling.
Exactly 8 % -- '<=' is inclusive (section 4), so PASS. Boundary guard.

The gel travels with the drink: G4b is one group and is FREE at every tier under v3.
An ordinary solid at the top-off -- FAIL H4. G1 is also AVOID there in the matrix; the form gate is what a composed-feeding harness will trip first.
The soft-solid allowance runs t-30 to about t-20, explicitly 'not in the last 15 minutes'. At t-10 the allowance lapses and the form gate applies -- FAIL H4.
The other named soft-solid: an applesauce pouch at t-25. Fibre 1.3 g is under the 2 g top-off ceiling anyway, so this passes without needing the H2 waiver.
Water is a valid answer to hydration and is never a valid top-off CARBOHYDRATE item -- FAIL H5.
Electrolyte powder: near-zero energy, zero carbohydrate -- FAIL H5. The athlete would believe they were fuelled. This is the failure mode H5 exists to catch.
Bran cereal at 9.0 g fibre against the snack's 4 g floor -- FAIL H2. This is the 'gross offender' H2 exists to catch, as opposed to whole-wheat bread at 3.8 g which it deliberately does not.
A berry-loaded bowl at 12.0 g fibre against the meal's 8 g floor -- FAIL H2 at 65 kg. Note it would PASS at 100 kg (0.12 * 100 = 12.0, inclusive); the gate scales by design.
30 g of protein at the snack tier against the 0.2 g/kg = 13 g ceiling -- FAIL H3. The snack ceiling is half the meal's; 'low-moderate protein' tightens as the window closes.
Same feeding that passes everything else, marked as never rehearsed -- FAIL H7. Thomas 2016: the pre-event meal 'should be well trialed and individualized'.
